metric.why: At AI rack densities, the coolant loop is the machine's life support. Flow loss or a supply-temperature excursion damages hardware in seconds to minutes, far faster than an air-cooled room degrades.
metric.metric: Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate
metric.target: Facility water loops commonly deliver warmer supply temperatures than comfort cooling, which is part of why liquid cooling improves PUE.
metric.definition: Supply and return temperature and flow rate of the coolant loop, whether direct-to-chip cold plates or immersion baths.

reading.body:
Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate are critical operational metrics for AI data centers because hardware damage occurs in seconds to minutes if the coolant loop fails, far faster than air-cooled systems degrade.

At the densities required for modern AI training, liquid cooling is not optional infrastructure but a direct dependency of compute availability. A supply-temperature excursion or flow loss does not gradually degrade performance. It stops the machine. This makes the coolant loop's stability a binding constraint on how much compute can run safely in a given facility, independent of how much power or space exists.

Liquid cooling also enables facilities to operate at higher supply temperatures than traditional air-cooled comfort cooling allows, which reduces the energy cost of cooling relative to compute output. This efficiency gain is why PUE improvements matter for AI scaling. The metric itself, supply and return temperature plus flow rate, is straightforward to instrument and monitor. What the data does not cover is variance in coolant chemistry, pump redundancy, or how loop failures cascade through a data center, nor does it address the water supply and sewage infrastructure that feeds these loops at scale.
